comments.body:
OWNED BY THIS EPIC ON FILE OVERLAP — AND ALREADY FIXED BY IT. Verified, not taken from the ticket text.

SCOPE: WE OWN IT. All three files this ticket declares in its file_impact were last modified by commit
`199b637b5` — "0a94: pin a UserIdentityModel contract" — which is story J4 of THIS epic
[rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85]:

    tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py                        -> 199b637b5
    tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_conflict_resolution.py    -> 199b637b5
    tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py -> 199b637b5

So the epic's work touched exactly the files this bug concerns. It stays parented here rather than
moving to a test-infrastructure epic. (My earlier reading — that this is generic pytest-loader work
with no Jira/DC dimension — was right about the SUBJECT but wrong about ownership: ownership follows
the edit-set, and the edit-set is ours.)

ALREADY FIXED, CONFIRMED TWO WAYS:

1. The helper is now CACHE-FIRST in all three files, not `setdefault`:
       cached = sys.modules.get(name)      # returns the REGISTERED module
       ...
       sys.modules[name] = mod             # not setdefault
   The defective form (`sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod)` followed by `return mod`, which returns a
   module that is NOT the registered one) is gone.

2. The ticket's OWN deterministic reproduction passes — the reversed collection order that made the
   defect fire:

       pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_conflict_resolution.py \
              tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py -q
       29 passed

   That ordering is the one that used to lose the `setdefault` race and produce
   `isinstance(Mutation(...), Mutation) is False`. It is green.

WHY IT WAS LATENT, which the ticket diagnosed correctly: alphabetical collection normally puts
`test_differ.py` first, so it won the `setdefault` and the suite was green; only a collection-order
flip (macOS vs Linux) exposed the two live copies of `mutation.py` under one `sys.modules` key.

Closing as `preexisting`: the defect pre-dated this epic (introduced with the test-package
subdivision, `5a87f5859`), was latent behind collection order, and was repaired as part of J4's work
on these files rather than by a dedicated change.

## REOPENED — this ticket closed WITHOUT a completion-verifier attestation

Operator ruling: a close without completion verification is prohibited. This ticket is `closed` with an empty `attestations` map — no `completion-verifier` record — so it never passed the gate.

**It is one of exactly two such tickets in epic e369's 41-descendant tree**, and together they are why the epic could not be certified. `gate_ops.py:129` sets `certifiable = not uncertified`, documented at the line:

> Certification is WITHHELD iff a direct child is closed-but-UNCERTIFIED (force-closed): the parent MAY close but cannot be certified — certification propagates, so an unattested descendant withholds the parent's signature.

So e369 closed with a PASS verdict and no signature, purely because this ticket and [rebar:2bc7-d77b-641c-42aa]/[rebar:0059-c7f0-cce1-4077] were unattested. Reopening is the documented remedy: move it back to `in_progress` and re-close through the gate, which mints the attestation and unblocks the epic's certification.

**Re-close it on its own merits, not to unblock the epic.** If its acceptance criteria are genuinely met the gate will say so; if they are not, that is a real finding and this ticket should stay open. Note the completion verifier has been repaired since these closes — [rebar:1019-e1e9-5117-4795] — so a re-close now runs a gate that can actually see.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## AUDIT-2BC7-A: the `setdefault` shape is GONE; the collision surface is much wider than this ticket assumed

Item 2 (audit the other shared by-path `sys.modules` keys) is the deliverable here, and it produced a
sharper picture than the ticket's framing. Done with an **AST walk**, not grep — see the method note.

### The original defect shape is fully eradicated

Zero real `sys.modules.setdefault` CALLS anywhere under `tests/`. The only two textual occurrences are
docstrings describing the historical defect (`test_applier_stale_binding_404.py`,
`test_load_module_identity.py`). So "setdefault-then-return-new" cannot recur today.

### But only 4 of 213 by-path loaders are cache-first

```
total by-path loaders under tests/ :  213
using setdefault (the old defect) :    0
cache-first (validated __file__)  :    4
```

The four are `test_differ.py`, `test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`,
`test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py` — **exactly the three files this ticket repaired** — plus
`test_reconcile_filter.py::_stub_modules`. Everything else registers into `sys.modules`
unconditionally.

### The `"mutation"` key is still loaded three ways it should not be

```
test_differ.py                     _load_module      cache-first
test_differ_conflict_resolution.py _load_module      cache-first
test_differ_quarantine_suppression _load_module      cache-first
test_differ_emits_probe.py         _load             UNGUARDED overwrite
test_apply_list_of_mutations.py    _load             name-only cache (no __file__ check)
test_mutation.py                   _load_mutation    UNGUARDED overwrite
```

So the repair covered 3 of the 6 registrants of the shared key. The remaining three are a **different**
failure mode from the original, not the same one: instead of keeping the old module and returning a new
one, they REPLACE another file's registration and return the replacement. Within a single file that is
self-consistent, which is why nothing fails today — pytest executes module-by-module and each file's
module-scoped fixture is built while its own registration is current. It is still the same
order-dependent coupling, and it is one collection-order change away from mattering.

`test_apply_list_of_mutations.py` deserves its own note: it caches on NAME only
(`if name in sys.modules: return sys.modules[name]`) with no `__file__` validation. That is the exact
"just cache on name" fix `test_load_module_identity.py` warns about — it can hand back a DIFFERENT
file's module registered under the same key.

### The wider surface, which the ticket did not anticipate

Keys registered by more than one file:

```
outbound_differ  9 files      reconcile           4 files
inbound_differ   8 files      mutation            6 files
differ           5 files      applier             3 files
```

None of the loaders for `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `reconcile` or `applier` is cache-first.
The original bug surfaced on `mutation` only because that is where a cross-file `isinstance` assertion
happened to exist; the same latent coupling is present on keys with twice as many registrants.

### Disposition of the three open items

* **Item 2 (audit) — DONE**, above.
* **Item 1 (shared conftest helper)** — still the right fix and NOT attempted here. The 6 registrants
  span `diffing/`, `mutate/` and `apply/`, and pytest puts only each test's OWN directory on
  `sys.path`, so a bare-name import of a shared helper does not resolve across them. Making it work
  needs either a `tests/`-root module plus path plumbing (the `_engine_path.py` pattern) or a conftest
  FIXTURE — and a fixture cannot serve the module-level constant call sites some of these files use.
  That is a real refactor across 200+ loaders, not a mechanical rename, and it should not ride on a
  bug whose subject was three files.
* **Item 3 (randomized order)** — recommendation, not applied: `pytest-randomly` would have caught
  this class locally instead of as a macOS-only surprise, but it makes every CI run's order differ,
  which converts *this* family of bug into an intermittent red. The defensible shape is a SEPARATE
  scheduled job that runs the suite with `-p randomly` and reports, leaving the per-commit lanes
  deterministic. That is a CI-policy decision, not an agent's call.

### Method note — my first scan was wrong and I nearly reported it

A regex-based scan reported "109 loaders with no cache-first guard". It was **an artifact**: my
function-body regex matched `(.*?)\):` for the argument list, which mis-parses every
`def f(...) -> Type:` signature and captured the wrong span. The AST numbers above supersede it. I
discarded the regex figure rather than reporting it; a scan's output is not evidence until the scan
itself is checked.

comments.body:
## CORRECTION-2BC7-B: one row of my audit table was wrong, and the correct value is more interesting

In AUDIT-2BC7-A I listed `test_mutation.py::_load_mutation` as an "UNGUARDED overwrite". **That is
wrong.** I built that table by hand from an earlier string-based heuristic instead of from the AST
walk whose numbers I quoted alongside it. Re-derived properly, per function:

```
file                                 func              registers?  shape
test_differ.py                       _load_module      yes         cache-first (name + __file__)
test_differ_conflict_resolution.py   _load_module      yes         cache-first (name + __file__)
test_differ_quarantine_suppression   _load_module      yes         cache-first (name + __file__)
test_differ_emits_probe.py           _load             yes         unconditional overwrite
test_apply_list_of_mutations.py      _load             yes         name-only cache, NO __file__ check
test_mutation.py                     _load_mutation    NO          UNREGISTERED private copy
test_differ.py (in-test loader)      test_diff_is_pure…NO          UNREGISTERED private copy (by design)
```

`_load_mutation` never touches `sys.modules` — it builds, execs and returns a module that is
**registered nowhere**. So it cannot clobber another file's registration, which is what I accused it of.

**Why the correct answer is worse to read than the wrong one.** "Returns an unregistered copy of
`mutation.py`" is this ticket's own TITLE — it is the exact shape of the original defect. The
difference is only that `_load_mutation` reaches it deliberately and in isolation: nothing in
`test_mutation.py` compares its objects against a class resolved out of `sys.modules`, so the two
copies never meet. It is safe by circumstance, not by construction. The moment a cell in that file
asserts `isinstance(x, <registered> Mutation)` — or a helper it calls resolves the class cache-first,
as `differ._load_mutation()` does — it reproduces 2bc7 exactly.

`test_differ.py`'s in-test loader is a genuine by-design exception: it registers under the distinct
name `mutation_for_diff_purity` precisely to get an isolated copy.

So the live unguarded registrants of the shared `"mutation"` key are **two**, not three:
`test_differ_emits_probe.py::_load` (unconditional overwrite) and
`test_apply_list_of_mutations.py::_load` (the name-only cache that
`test_load_module_identity.py`'s docstring explicitly warns about — it can return a DIFFERENT file's
module registered under the same key).

The rest of AUDIT-2BC7-A stands: zero real `setdefault` calls remain, 4 of 213 by-path loaders are
cache-first, and the `outbound_differ` / `inbound_differ` / `reconcile` / `applier` keys have 9 / 8 / 4
/ 3 registrants respectively with no cache-first loader among them.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py` fails with

    AssertionError: assert False
      where False = isinstance(Mutation(direction=..., action=..., target='DSO-42', ...),
                               <class 'mutation.Mutation'>)

i.e. an object that IS a `Mutation` fails `isinstance` against `Mutation`. Observed on
`macos-latest / py3.13` in CI while `ubuntu-latest / py3.13` — same Python version — passed, which is the
signature of a collection-order dependency rather than a version or logic defect.

## Root cause (reproduced deterministically, not inferred)

Five test files load `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mutation.py` **by path** under the SHARED
`sys.modules` key `"mutation"`:

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_mutation.py`

Three of them shared this helper:

    def _load_module(name: str, path: Path) -> ModuleType:
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod)   # keeps an EARLIER registration
        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
        return mod                          # ...but returns the NEW module

`setdefault` keeps whatever was registered first, yet the function returns the freshly-created module. So
whenever another file has already registered `"mutation"`, the fixture hands back a module object that is
**not** `sys.modules["mutation"]` — two live copies of the same source, with two distinct `Mutation` classes.

Meanwhile `differ._load_mutation()` resolves its `Mutation` cache-first out of `sys.modules` (checking
`"mutation"`, `"rebar_reconciler.mutation"`, …). So the differ builds objects from copy A while the test
asserts against copy B, and `isinstance` is correctly `False`.

Whichever file pytest collects first wins the `setdefault`, so the outcome depends on collection order —
which differs between macOS and Linux.

**Deterministic reproduction** (fails before the fix, passes after):

    pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_conflict_resolution.py \
           tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py -q

The natural alphabetical order puts `test_differ.py` first, so it normally wins and the suite is green; that
is why this sat latent.

## Fix (landed with story J4, `0a94-e104-7304-4d85`)

Make the helper cache-first, so the returned module always IS the registered one — mirroring what
`differ._load_mutation()` already does:

    cached = sys.modules.get(name)
    if cached is not None and getattr(cached, "__file__", None) == str(path):
        return cached
    ...
    sys.modules[name] = mod

Applied to the three `setdefault`-based helpers. `test_differ_emits_probe.py` already assigned
unconditionally (self-consistent) and `test_mutation.py` loads inline, so neither carried the defect.

## Why it was bundled with J4 rather than landed separately

J4 added two test files, which perturbed macOS collection order enough to make another registrant win the
race — turning a latent landmine into a `Verified -1` that blocked J4's own change. The fix therefore had to
sit at or below J4 in the review stack for J4 to go green. It is test-only, ~6 lines across three files, and
the alternative (a separate change spliced beneath an already-pushed one, blocking on its own plan review)
bought nothing. The bundling is disclosed in J4's commit message rather than smuggled.

## Remaining work this ticket tracks

- [x] Consider a shared conftest helper so the by-path loader exists ONCE instead of being copy-pasted into
      five test modules — the duplication is what let three copies carry the same defect
- [x] Audit the other shared by-path `sys.modules` keys (`differ`, `config`, `adf`, `outbound_fields`,
      `comment_limits`) for the same `setdefault`-then-return-new shape
- [x] Consider making CI run the suite in a randomized order (e.g. `pytest-randomly`) so order-dependent
      coupling fails fast and locally rather than as a platform-specific surprise

## Disposition of the three items (session AUDIT-2BC7-A / CORRECTION-2BC7-B)

**Audit — DONE.** AST walk over `tests/`: zero real `sys.modules.setdefault` calls remain, so the
original shape is eradicated. But only 4 of 213 by-path loaders are cache-first, and the
`outbound_differ` / `inbound_differ` / `differ` / `reconcile` / `applier` keys have 9 / 8 / 5 / 4 / 3
registrants with no cache-first loader among them. Two live unguarded registrants of the shared
`"mutation"` key were fixed here (Gerrit 1380); the wider surface is filed as
[rebar:e351-537e-a9ca-4669].

**Shared conftest helper — CONSIDERED, deferred with reasons, follow-up filed.** It is the right fix
and it is not mechanical: the registrants span seven directories and pytest puts only each test's OWN
directory on `sys.path`, so a bare-name import does not resolve across them. The two workable shapes
(a `tests/`-root module plus the `_engine_path.py` path plumbing, or a conftest fixture that cannot
serve module-level call sites) are recorded on e351 with acceptance criteria, including a guard test
so the count cannot regress silently.

**Randomized collection order — CONSIDERED, recommendation recorded, not applied.**
`pytest-randomly` would have caught this class locally rather than as a macOS-only surprise, but it
makes every CI run's order differ, converting this family of bug into an intermittent red. The
defensible shape is a SEPARATE scheduled job running with randomization while the per-commit lanes
stay deterministic. That is a CI-policy decision, so it is recorded rather than taken unilaterally.
